newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas risies, centres on day ahead and July year.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas risies, centres on day ahead and July year.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas markets saw trade concentrated on the year from July and on the day ahead on Tuesday with prices marginally firmer for most periods, traders and brokers said.

One buyer confirmed buying over 100,000 therms a day of gas in the year starting from July, all at the same price, 12.70 pence a therm. But full details were only given concerning 50,000 th/d of this, in two separate deals. And there was another July year trade, involving a different buyer, at 12.7125 pence a therm.

Otherwise, the main focus of the day remained the day ahead market. With persistent rumours heard about problems either at Bacton terminal or offshore at a field delivering to Bacton, there was keen interest for day ahead gas at higher prices.

Deals were heard as high as 10.70 pence a therm, considerably higher than Monday's level. And there were rumours of a single trade at 10.35 pence for 200,000 therms, but this was not confirmed - although a total of 245,000 therms at between 10.40 and 10.70 pence was confirmed by various different players.

In other periods trade on the physical market was thin and quiet. Interest on the IPE futures market was, unusually, greater than on the OTC, and prices rose as far forward as September before falling back in the mainly untraded later months. 525 lots were traded, the third highest total since the contract began, with most of the activity done in June and July which between them accounted for 305 lots.

Transco announced on Tuesday evening that the temperature forecast for Wednesday is 9.2 Celsius against a seasonal normal 9.7 Celsius, and demand is expected to reach 224 mcm, 52 percent of peak day demand.
